tateti.name: Tic-Tac-Toe
tateti.description: Classic 3×3: win with 3 in a row, unlimited pieces and no moving them.

titeta.name: Titeta
titeta.description: 3×3 misère: complete 3 in a row and you lose. Max 3 pieces per player, forced mode (move oldest when full).

bullet.name: Bullet
bullet.description: Classic tic-tac-toe with a 60-second total bank per player.

quebrantasuelos.name: Quebrantasuelos
quebrantasuelos.description: 4×4: when you move, the square you leave stays broken for 3 turns times the number of players.

geocentrismo.name: Geocentrismo
geocentrismo.description: 4×4 with gravity: every 1 turn per player it rotates 90° clockwise and pieces settle again.

movementInfo.title: Movement types
movementInfo.intro: These modes change legal destinations when a placed piece is allowed to move.
movementInfo.guideSelect: First choose one of your pieces; then only destinations compatible with the selected pattern are highlighted.
movementInfo.guideBlocked: Pieces, broken cells, and board edges can block line-based movement.
movementInfo.guideEffects: Eat removes enemy pieces; Capture converts them. If both are off, jumps do not affect the jumped piece.
movementInfo.effects: Eat and Capture are mutually exclusive. Capture only applies to Checker, Horseman, and Mage.

modes.normal: Adds no restriction: any legal empty destination remains allowed.
modes.king: Moves exactly 1 cell in any direction.
modes.grandKing: Moves up to 2 cells in any direction.
modes.queen: Moves in a straight horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line without passing through pieces or broken cells.
modes.rook: Moves horizontally or vertically without passing through pieces or broken cells.
modes.pillar: Moves exactly 1 horizontal or vertical cell.
modes.bishop: Moves diagonally without passing through pieces or broken cells.
modes.knight: Moves in an L shape like a chess knight.
modes.neon: Moves 1 horizontal or vertical cell. If Eat is enabled, it can also eat 1 diagonal cell.
modes.checkers: Moves 1 diagonal cell. It can jump an enemy piece to the next diagonal cell if that cell is free.
modes.horsemen: Moves 1 horizontal or vertical cell. It can jump an enemy piece in a straight line if the next cell is free.
modes.mage: Combines Checker and Horseman: moves or jumps diagonally, horizontally, or vertically.

general.title: General
general.html:
This is where you define the match foundation: board size, objective, and the line length that decides the result.

What you can configure

  • N Columns and N Rows change the board width and height.
  • Win / Lose decides whether completing a line makes you win or lose.
  • N in a row defines how many consecutive pieces trigger that condition.

How it changes the game

  • A larger board gives more room for variants with gravity, blocking, or collapse.
  • If you choose Lose, you play misère mode: completing a line becomes something to avoid.
  • The line length must fit on the board; the app limits it according to rows and columns.

pieces.title: Pieces
pieces.html:
This is where you decide how many pieces each player has and whether placed pieces can move again.

What you can configure

  • Unlimited on lets players place pieces without a cap; off uses the quantity field.
  • Quantity is the maximum number of live pieces per player when pieces are not unlimited.
  • Move pieces defines when a piece may move: never, only after reaching the limit, or freely.
  • Movement appears when movement is allowed and adds patterns such as King, Rook, Checker, or Knight.
  • Eat removes enemy pieces reached by the pattern; Capture converts them to your own pieces when the mode supports it.

How it changes the game

  • With few pieces, order matters: the number on each piece shows which one was placed first.
  • Forced modes push the match toward recycling pieces; free modes make it more tactical.
  • Special patterns change which destinations are legal, so the info button next to Movement explains each one.

holes.title: Rupture
holes.html:
Rupture makes a cell unusable after a piece leaves it.

What you can configure

  • The title switch enables or disables this mechanic.
  • Turns sets how long the rupture lasts from the next turn onward.
  • Unlimited keeps the broken cell blocked until the match ends.
  • Per player multiplies the duration by the number of active players when the match is configured.

How it changes the game

  • If disabled, moving a piece leaves the cell immediately available.
  • If enabled, movement has a spatial cost: you can close paths or block areas.
  • Broken cells also interfere with line movement and gravity.

gravity.title: Gravity
gravity.html:
Gravity pulls every piece toward one side of the board, as if that side were the floor.

What you can configure

  • The title switch enables or disables gravity.
  • Initial direction sets where pieces fall at the start.
  • Rotate gravity can change the direction after a number of turns or rounds.
  • Rotation step chooses how much gravity turns each time: 90°, 180°, 270°, or random.
  • Turn direction sets clockwise, counter-clockwise, or random rotation.

How to play with gravity

  • When placing, tap an empty cell in the column or row: the piece falls to its landing spot.
  • Strong arrows show where the piece will land; faint arrows are shortcuts in the same fall line.
  • When moving a piece, choose an empty cell and then the whole board settles in the current direction.
  • Broken cells act as obstacles and can split a column or row into separate segments.
  • When gravity rotates, there is a short pause before pieces settle again.

players.title: Players
players.html:
This is where you choose how many players join and how matches with more than two players resolve.

What you can configure

  • Number of players uses the first players in the list, in that turn order.
  • With more than two players in Lose mode, Eliminate losers can clear their pieces when they are removed.
  • With more than two players in Win mode, Continue for ranking lets play continue after the first winner.
  • If ranking continues, Eliminate winners decides whether a winner's pieces are removed or kept as obstacles.

How it changes the game

  • In two-player matches, winning or losing ends the match normally.
  • In three-or-more-player matches, elimination options decide whether the board partially clears or keeps pieces that affect the remaining players.
  • Player icons and colors are edited from the players panel.

clock.title: Clock
clock.html:
The clock adds time pressure to each player.

What you can configure

  • The title switch enables or disables the clock.
  • Total bank gives each player one time budget for the whole match.
  • Recover on move adds seconds after a legal move, without exceeding the initial bank.
  • Per-turn clock resets the same allowance for every move.

How it changes the game

  • In total bank mode, if the timer reaches 0, that player loses or is eliminated depending on player count.
  • In per-turn mode, if the timer reaches 0, only that move is forfeited and play passes on.
  • During the gravity-rotation pause, the clock does not run.

restrictions.title: Blocking
restrictions.html:
Blocking reserves cells that cannot be used at the start of the match.

What you can configure

  • The title switch enables or disables opening blocked cells.
  • For N defines how long they stay blocked.
  • Unit lets that time count in turns or rounds.
  • Edit blocked cells opens a grid matching the current board so you can paint and unpaint cells.

How it changes the game

  • While blocking lasts, new pieces cannot be placed on painted cells.
  • When the countdown ends, those cells become available again.
  • The board event indicator shows when blocking will release.

collapse.title: Collapse
collapse.html:
Collapse shrinks the board by breaking edges at scheduled moments.

What you can configure

  • The title switch enables or disables the mechanic.
  • Type chooses which edge or edges break: left, right, up, down, horizontal, vertical, or circular.
  • Every N and Unit define the interval in turns or rounds.
  • Times limits how many collapses can happen during the match.
  • Kill players decides whether a player left without pieces by collapse loses or keeps playing.

How it changes the game

  • Each collapse advances one layer inward; for example, circular breaks the next ring of the board.
  • Collapsed cells stay broken until the end of the match.
  • If there were pieces on those cells, they are destroyed when the collapse happens.
  • The event indicator warns when the next collapse is coming.

restrictionGrid.intro: Paint the cells where pieces cannot be placed while opening blocking is active.
